'''Karin Liltorp''' (born 6 May 1972) is a Danish politician and a [[member of the Folketing]] for [[Copenhagen (Folketing constituency)|Copenhagen]] from the [[Moderates (Denmark)|Moderates]]. Alongside sixteen other members of the [[Moderates (Denmark)|Moderates]], Liltorp was elected to the [[Folketing]] in [[2022 Danish general election|November 2022]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Karin Liltorp |url=https://www.thedanishparliament.dk/members/karin-liltorp |access-date=2023-11-01 |website=The Danish Parliament |language=en}}</ref> She was her party's spokesperson on [[Environmental law|global environment]], [[higher education]], [[Science policy|research]] and the [[European Union]].<ref name=":0" /> In February 2025, she announced she was leaving the party.<ref>{{cite news |title= Folketingsmedlem melder sig ud af Moderaterne |url=https://jyllands-posten.dk/politik/ECE17931517/folketingsmedlem-melder-sig-ud-af-moderaterne/ |access-date=23 February 2025 |work=[[Jyllands-Posten]] |date=23 February 2025 |language=da}}</ref> She joined [[The Alternative (Denmark)|the Alternative]] a short time later.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-04 |title=Folketingsmedlem Karin Liltorp melder sig ind i Alternativet |url=https://www.dr.dk/nyheder/seneste/folketingsmedlem-karin-liltorp-melder-sig-ind-i-alternativet |access-date=2025-03-13 |website=DR |language=da-DK}}</ref>
